writer.markdown:
## Company overview

NVIDIA Corporation is a Technology sector company in the Semiconductors industry, describing itself as a data center scale AI infrastructure company. It sells in the United States, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, Europe and internationally. Its business has two segments. Compute & Networking provides accelerated computing and networking platforms, AI solutions and software, and automotive platforms including autonomous and electric vehicle solutions. Graphics offers GeForce GPUs for gaming and PCs and Quadro/NVIDIA RTX GPUs for enterprise workstations. The market capitalisation is $5.65T, and the shares trade at 233.95, near the top of a 52-week range of 164.27-237.88.

## Financial commentary

Revenue has grown rapidly, from $26.97B in fiscal 2023 to $60.92B in 2024, $130.50B in 2025 and $215.94B in 2026. Net income rose even faster, from $4.37B to $29.76B, then $72.88B, and $120.07B in fiscal 2026. The result is a net margin of 63.7%, and the latest revenue growth figure is 105.9%.

Returns and leverage are also strong. Return on equity is 117.2% and debt to equity is 0.17. The dividend yield is a modest 0.4%. Recent news noted a $150 billion increase to the share repurchase authorization.

## Comps commentary

Peers are AMD, Broadcom, Intel, Marvell and Qualcomm. On the primary measure, forward P/E, NVIDIA sits at 14.9 against a peer median of 40.3, which is 63% lower. Trailing P/E of 29.6 is 56% below the peer median of 67.7. EV/EBITDA of 27.9 is 26% below the median of 37.9, and EV/Revenue of 18.5 is only 5% below the median of 19.4.

The operating comparison is much more favourable. Net margin of 63.7% is 203% above the peer median of 21.0%, and revenue growth of 105.9% is 190% above the median of 36.5%. Debt to equity of 0.17 is 65% below the median of 0.49. In short, the company screens cheaper than peers on most earnings-based multiples while showing stronger growth and profitability. Peer dispersion is wide, so the median should be read with care.

## Risk commentary

The three most severe risks all carry the top severity score of 3. First, shifting and expanding US export controls over the past three years have limited the company's ability to serve customers outside the United States. Second, competition could adversely affect market share and financial results. Third, long manufacturing lead times, uncertain supply and capacity, and inaccurate demand estimates have caused and could again cause mismatches between supply and demand.

Three further risks are rated 2. The company relies on outside suppliers to manufacture, assemble, test or package its products, which reduces control over quantity, quality, yields and delivery schedules. It must keep pace with changing industry and market needs. International sales and operations are a significant part of the business and carry their own exposures. The recent news flow, centred on the buyback and investor purchases, does not relate directly to these risks.
